title: Thirteen Down
tagline: Thirteen in reserve. Four to build. One bloom to finish.
teaser: Canfield, the solitaire with a reputation: a tough reserve of thirteen, foundations that start wherever the deal decides, and every peek at the deck costing you points. Dealt on a deck of cards drawn entirely in code.

inspiredBy.uiTitle: the Berkeley solitaire with a bank account

manPage.synopsis: thirteen down — empty a reserve of thirteen and build four foundations up in suit from the deal's base card; every peek has its price.
manPage.description: Steve Levine wrote Canfield for Berkeley's machines; Steve Feldman, Kirk McKusick, Mikey Olson and Eric Allman kept working on it, and Kirk McKusick gave it an account that charged for the deal, for every look at the cards and for every minute at the table, and kept everyone's balance in one shared file. Thirteen Down plays its rules exactly, keeps the price of information, and lets you choose points or the old account in play money.

howToPlay: Build four foundations up in suit, starting from the deal's base card and turning the corner from king to ace.
Build the four tableau piles down in alternating colours; whole piles move together, and only the reserve fills a space.
Deal the hand to the talon three at a time. Insight shows the cards you have seen, at a price.
